texts: bad: "several vessels full of mire-essence" cannot be recorded as written — the fullness belongs to each vessel, but inside a generic about days the vessels are a fresh batch minted per day, and we have no way to hand a property to the members of such a batch, so the parse ends up saying the collection as a whole is full (which is not what you mean) and the per-vessel reading is lost either way. Move the essence into the verb so no member-property is needed: "Typical days fill several vessels with mire-essence." — the count still rides on the vessels and the mire-essence is carried as what they are filled with.

mixed: the rule fires and the count of four is kept, but the same "four vessels full of mire-essence" problem applies — the fullness of each vessel has no place to attach on a per-day batch of vessels, so that half is dropped. Rewrite it the same way as the previous sentence: "Heavy-thread days fill four vessels with mire-essence." (Separately, the translator also asserted that heavy-thread days are themselves "heavy", reading the "heavy" out of your two-word term; that is our slip, not your sentence's — the compliant parse just omits it — so keep "heavy-thread days" as one term, since it is what keeps the rule fireable.)

mixed: everything works except "a single" — it came out as a quality of the vessel ("the vessel is single") instead of a count, because our counting machinery only counts groups and has nowhere to put an exact count on one object; the "full of mire-essence" half is fine here, since the bearer is one vessel and not a batch. Minimal fix: "Thin days yield one vessel full of mire-essence." — the lone vessel then carries the "one" as far as the notation can. If the contrast with typical and heavy-thread days is the point of the sentence, state it as a comparison in its own sentence ("A thin day fills fewer vessels than a typical day."), which we can record.

good. the whenever-rule fires: the wraith and the lantern are plain variables any later draining event can match, the falling harvest is minted once per occurrence and tied to its trigger, and the harvest is typed and placed at that same lantern.
